newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police detain man in police murder probe.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police detain man in police murder probe.

text.p: Northern Ireland police have arrested a man for questioning about the IRA killings of two police officers in Lurgan town last week, security sources said on Tuesday.

Irish Republican Army gunmen shot dead two patrolmen in the County Armagh town last Monday, throwing peace efforts in the troubled province into disarray and heightening tension in the run-up to the climax of disputed pro-British street parades.
A man detained last week was subsequently released. "There has been one more arrest in relation to the Lurgan murders," a police source said on Tuesday.

The killings, part of a long-running IRA campaign aimed at forcing an end to British rule in Northern Ireland, outraged Prime Minister Tony Blair and provoked outright condemnation of the republican extremists by U.S. President Bill Clinton and the outgoing Irish Prime Minister John Bruton.

Britain abruptly severed low-level contacts with Sinn Fein, the IRA's political arm. Blair planned a parliamentary statement on Wednesday on his recently elected Labour government's efforts for peace in the province.
Britain says that Sinn Fein will be invited to peace talks only when the IRA renounces violence.
London and Dublin say they have agreed a joint stance on the vexed question of how to achieve guerrilla disarmament in the event of an future IRA ceasefire.
The deal is aimed at overcoming a 17-month impasse in Belfast talks from which Sinn Fein is barred.
